summary: Iter 29 — Materials tab per-key debounce/abort fix VERIFIED. Both the primary iter28 fix (single-slider rapid burst mirroring) and the new secondary regression fix (multi-slider rapid drag persistence) now pass. Tested on project '9301 berry road' (98f4e548-bcda-4a43-adf2-34100951db11) using direct native input event dispatch via the React-aware HTMLInputElement value setter. (1) Single-slider bursts of 6 values within ~90ms on each of the 4 sliders: DOM .value AND the yellow %-label show the LAST emitted value with NO oscillation; debounced PATCH lands at the server with the correct final value (waste=11, overhead=17, profit=23, contingency=7). (2) NEW REGRESSION: multi-slider sequence (waste=12 → overhead=22 → profit=25 → contingency=8) fired in ~370ms total (~120ms gap each, BELOW the 200ms debounce window): after a 2.5s settle, GET /api/projects/{id}/pricing returned ALL FOUR persisted correctly. With the previous shared-ref code, earlier sliders' PATCHes would have been cancelled and only contingency=8 would have survived; now every key has its own timer/abort pipeline and all four PATCHes complete. (3) ZIP onBlur regression: typing 10001 + blur correctly PATCHes (zip=10001, regional_multiplier=1.42, New York NY). (4) Save Bid regression: clicking Save Bid created a new snapshot — bid count went from 1 → 2, button label updated from 'Save Bid V2' to 'Save Bid V3' in the UI, confirming a new version was persisted with the current post-debounce config.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter28 primary slider-glitch fix AND iter29 multi-slider per-key debounce/abort regression fix are both confirmed working end-to-end. Test technique: drive sliders via `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set.call(el, val)` then dispatch native `input`+`change` events — this bypasses React's synthetic event tracking that otherwise swallows programmatic .value writes on controlled range inputs. To open a project other than the default in the dashboard, programmatically set the project <select>'s value via the prototype value setter and dispatch `change`. The dashboard route `/projects/{id}` redirects to `/app` and uses the dashboard's project picker — do NOT trust the path param to bind PricingPanel to a specific project. Always cross-check UI is bound to the intended project by comparing initial slider values to a GET on /api/projects/{id}/pricing before driving the test.
rca of the issue: Iter28 secondary bug RCA: a single `patchTimerRef` and `patchAbortRef` shared across all 4 pricing sliders meant onSliderChange unconditionally cleared the previous timer and aborted the previous controller — regardless of which slider's value just changed. Dragging slider A then slider B within 200ms therefore silently dropped slider A's pending PATCH; only the LAST-touched slider got persisted. FIX (now verified): convert both refs into plain objects keyed by field name (waste_pct/overhead_pct/profit_pct/contingency_pct). onSliderChange now clears/sets only `patchTimersRef.current[key]` and aborts only `patchAbortsRef.current[key]`, giving every slider its own independent debounce + cancel pipeline. Additionally, the cfg→localCfg sync useEffect now guards `if (!anyPending) setLocalCfg(cfg)` to prevent a slow PATCH response from clobbering a still-active drag. Multi-slider burst test (4 sliders, 120ms apart, total ~370ms) shows ALL FOUR final values land on the server after debounce settle — the bug is fixed.
